papers.title: Distribution-Free Prediction Sets for Two-Layer Hierarchical Models
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 118(544):2491-2502 (arXiv 1809.07441, first posted 2018)
papers.authors: Robin Dunn, Larry Wasserman, Aaditya Ramdas
papers.why: The canonical treatment of the group (patient/site), not the record, as the exchangeable unit for distribution-free prediction — CDF pooling, single subsampling, repeated subsampling. It is prediction-set coverage, not certified selective risk, but it is THE classic for CertGate's site-as-unit exchangeability premise; a statistics-literate reviewer will expect it cited.

papers.title: Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data
papers.venue: ACM Journal of Data Science (accepted 2025-12-18; arXiv 2306.06342)
papers.authors: Yonghoon Lee, Rina Foygel Barber, et al.
papers.why: Formalizes hierarchical exchangeability and extends conformal prediction and jackknife+ to grouped/repeated-measurement data, including second-moment (dispersion-aware) coverage — directly adjacent to CertGate's site-population-average estimand plus between-site-dispersion clause. Coverage guarantees, not selective-risk certificates.

papers.title: When Average Calibration Fails: Site-Conditional Federated Conformal Risk Control (via Risk-Curve Shrinkage)
papers.why: Treats hospitals/institutions as calibration units in federated conformal risk control on medical (FeTS-2022 brain-tumor) data and shows pooled CRC protects the average hospital while violating coverage at 40% of individual institutions — the same aggregate-vs-individual signature CertGate measures in E1/E6, and finite-sample corrections are shown load-bearing. No selective prediction/abstention, no betting certificate; segmentation, not clinical risk scores.

papers.title: Certify or Refuse: A Cross-Model Map for Selective Risk Control with Coverage Floors under Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Jiamiao Liu, Dewen Qiao, Yu Zhang, Xuetao Chen
papers.why: Certified selective prediction under distribution shift with labeled-source + unlabeled-target resources and an honest-refusal feasibility frontier — conceptually parallel to CertGate's decline-rather-than-overclaim discipline and its BBSE-mode budget, but for covariate (not label) shift, record-level i.i.d. units, NLP experiments, no clinical data, no site clustering.

papers.title: A Joint Finite-Sample Certificate for Adaptive Selective Conformal Risk Control
papers.why: A single finite-sample certificate jointly bounding selected risk, acceptance probability, and utility under adaptive threshold selection — overlaps CertGate's component (2) headline (finite-sample certified selective risk) closely. Record-level exchangeability on vision benchmarks (ImageNet/COCO/ADE20K); no clustered data, no clinical setting, no e-value/betting machinery.

papers.title: Selective Conformal Risk Control
papers.authors: Yunpeng Xu, Wenge Guo, Zhi Wei
papers.why: Selective prediction with conformal risk control giving finite-sample selective and marginal guarantees for general continuous risks — the same guarantee family as CertGate's answered-error bound, via conformal rather than betting/e-value machinery, with the record as the unit and no multi-site or clinical component.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Confirmation of Label-Shift Corrections
papers.why: Shows the likelihood ratio between a label-shift-corrected predictive and the source predictive is a conditional e-value, giving an anytime-valid (Ville) confirmation rule for label-shift corrections — the intersection of CertGate's components (2) e-value/martingale and (3) label shift, but for confirming a pre-specified correction in GP regression simulations; no selective prediction, no clustered clinical data, no BBSE estimation.

papers.title: Distribution-free uncertainty quantification for classification under label shift
papers.why: The classic for distribution-free UQ under label shift with importance-weight (BBSE-style) correction and explicit handling of weight-estimation uncertainty — the direct ancestor of CertGate's BBSE mode with an honest q_t budget. Coverage, not selective-risk certification, and record-level units.

papers.title: Tracking the risk of a deployed model and detecting harmful distribution shifts
papers.why: Sequential testing / confidence-sequence (betting-adjacent) machinery to certify that a deployed model's risk has not harmfully increased — the closest classic to CertGate's use of anytime-valid wealth arguments for deployed-model error control. No abstention layer, no cluster-as-unit structure; a methods reviewer from the SAVI community would expect it in related work.

papers.title: Conformal selective prediction with cost-aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
papers.why: Clinical selective prediction combining conformal finite-sample coverage with cost-aware deferral to clinicians under distribution shift (PhysioNet 2019 sepsis, not eICU) — overlaps the clinical-selective-prediction-with-guarantees lane a health-informatics reviewer patrols, but coverage-of-sets rather than answered-error certification, temporal (not site) shift, no hospital-as-unit treatment.

papers.title: A Self-Adaptive Mixup-Augmented Selective Prediction Framework: A Case Study on In-Hospital Mortality Prediction
papers.venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics 30(7):5642-5655; doi:10.1109/JBHI.2025.3639425 (via PubMed, PMID 41329580)
papers.authors: Kaidi Gong, Yuan Xu, Xiaolei Xie
papers.why: Selective prediction (learned abstention) for ICU in-hospital mortality with uncertainty-plus-interpretation integration — the same task and abstention framing as CertGate's application, and it pairs abstention with explanation as CertGate's component (4) does. Empirical selective-risk reduction only: no finite-sample certificate, no site-level statistics, no pre-registered protocol.

papers.title: A hierarchical conformal framework for uncertainty-aware length of stay prediction in multi-hospital settings
papers.authors: Marzieh Amiri Shahbazi, Ali Baheri, Nasibeh Azadeh-Fard
papers.why: Explicitly treats hospitals as clustering units for conformal calibration in healthcare (HCUP NIS, 3,793 hospitals), deploying the Dunn et al. two-layer schemes (CDF pooling / subsampling) plus Bayesian uncertainty — the nearest published multi-hospital-conformal-in-healthcare neighbor. Interval coverage for LOS regression, primary method carries no finite-sample guarantee, no abstention, no certification.

papers.title: Selective Omniprediction and Fair Abstention
papers.why: (C,G)-multigroup selective classification with provable per-group abstention guarantees — theoretical context for group-level abstention fairness; multicalibration-style guarantees over subpopulations, not cluster-sampling independence, and no clinical or finite-sample-certificate component.

papers.title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
papers.venue: JAMA Network Open 8(6):e2513685; doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.13685 (via PubMed, PMID 40465297)
papers.authors: Vallijah Subasri, Amrit Krishnan, et al. (Verma, Goldenberg, Dolatabadi)
papers.why: Label-agnostic monitoring of a multi-hospital in-hospital-mortality model using a black-box shift estimator (BBSE) with MMD testing across 7 Toronto hospitals — real-world clinical use of CertGate's BBSE ingredient, but for drift detection and retraining, with no certification, abstention, or site-level statistical guarantee.

papers.title: Calibration Drift Under Cross-Institutional Deployment: An External Validation Framework for ICU Mortality Prediction Across MIMIC-IV and eICU
papers.why: An eICU-based external-validation framework for ICU mortality (MIMIC-IV develop, eICU 114,060-stay validate; calibration metrics, recalibration, APACHE benchmarking, fairness audit) — occupies the eICU cross-institution validation lane and documents the prevalence/label-shift failure CertGate's mode 2 targets, but is descriptive: no statistical guarantee, no abstention, no site-as-unit inference.
